candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide care and education related to normal pregnancy, prenatal health promotion, screening, health maintenance and prevention of complications.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — purpose and individualized delivery of prenatal care
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that prenatal care supports maternal-fetal monitoring, screening, education, counseling, and social-resource assessment throughout pregnancy, while the frequency and format of visits may be individualized according to current risk and care needs.

options.A: Prenatal care provides ongoing maternal and fetal monitoring, screening and testing, education, and support, while the visit schedule can be adjusted to the client's medical and social needs.
options.B: Prenatal care is mainly beneficial for clients already classified as high risk; uncomplicated pregnancies require little routine monitoring or education.
options.C: Prenatal care is effective only when every pregnant client follows the same fixed number and timing of in-person visits regardless of risk or preferences.
options.D: Once telehealth is available, in-person prenatal visits are generally unnecessary because physical examinations and laboratory testing can be completed remotely.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current ACOG guidance describes prenatal care as including medical care, screening tests, monitoring of maternal and fetal health, counseling, education, and help with social support and community resources. ACOG's 2025 Clinical Consensus on tailored prenatal care states that visit frequency and monitoring may be individualized according to medical and social needs rather than using one rigid schedule for everyone. B is incorrect because routine prenatal care is relevant to both average-risk and high-risk pregnancies. C is incorrect because ACOG now specifically supports tailored visit schedules for appropriate clients. D is incorrect because telehealth can supplement prenatal care, but in-person visits remain necessary when physical examination, laboratory testing, imaging, or other hands-on services are required.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Ongoing prenatal care provides maternal-fetal monitoring, screening/testing, education and support, while current ACOG guidance permits tailoring visit frequency and modality to medical, social and individual care needs.
candidate.source_document_title: Prenatal Care; Tailored Prenatal Care Delivery for Pregnant Individuals
candidate.source_locator: ACOG Prenatal Care FAQ — 'What is prenatal care?': prenatal care may include medical care, screening tests, answers to questions, social support and community resources; prenatal visits monitor the pregnant person's and fetus's health and include routine measurements/testing. 'What is tailored prenatal care?' and 'How often should I expect to go into the office?': care is individualized by complication risk, preferences and health needs. ACOG Clinical Consensus, Tailored Prenatal Care Delivery — Frequency: visit frequency and monitoring schedule may be tailored to medical and social needs; targeted schedules can provide equivalent outcomes for selected average-risk individuals.
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
candidate.source_version_date: ACOG Prenatal Care FAQ current page accessed 2026-08-17; ACOG Clinical Consensus, April 2025, current page accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A pregnant client asks why ongoing prenatal care is important if the number and type of visits can be tailored to individual needs. Which response by the nurse is best?
